text: To the GPU: the same ideas with the dials turned Everything above carries over to GPUs: SIMD becomes SIMT (a warp of 32 threads runs one instruction together, written as scalar code per thread), cache lines become coalescing (a warp should read neighbouring addresses), a mispredicted branch becomes divergence (both paths run in turn), and the roofline's ridge moves far right, so LLM decode is even more memory-bound.

text: The mapping, row by row Idea on the CPU (this page) Its GPU counterpart A few large cores with big caches, branch predictors and out-of-order execution, built to make one thread fast Thousands of simple lanes, built for throughput; little cache per lane, no out-of-order execution Latency hidden by caches and the prefetcher Latency hidden by switching between many groups of threads while some wait for memory SIMD: one instruction on 4 lanes (NEON), written as vectors SIMT: groups of 32 threads (a warp) run one instruction together, written as scalar code per thread Cache lines: read neighbours together Coalescing: the threads of a warp should read neighbouring addresses A branch mispredicted costs a pipeline flush Threads of a warp that take different branches run both paths, one after the other (divergence) Register blocking, cache tiling Shared-memory tiling, tensor cores Roofline with about 100 GB/s and 0.5 TFLOP/s on this laptop's CPU The same model at TB/s and hundreds of TFLOP/s: the ridge is further right Atomics and memory orders between threads The same, plus scopes (block, device, system)
